topics.flagship-ru-ua: Ukrainian officials raised the death toll from the Zaporizhia aid strike to at least 50, with DNA tests being used to identify bodies and up to 39 people reportedly still under rubble. Ursula von der Leyen is set to visit the Black Sea after at least seven commercial vessels were reportedly struck by drones that many link to Russia. On the diplomatic track, three-way Ukraine-Russia-US talks are due in Abu Dhabi next week. Zelenskiy is seeking concrete Western commitments first, NATO is calling for a "just and sustainable" end to the war, and the Oleshky ceasefire was praised by envoys at a White House event. Single-source items include satellite imagery of a new Russian attack-drone launch base with eight bays and reports from Odesa of performances continuing under missile alerts.
topics.flagship-ir-il: President Trump is reportedly weighing renewed strikes on Iran despite a midterm defeat that has prompted public criticism from VP Vance and an impeachment push against Defense Secretary Hegseth. Energy consultancy FGE NexantECA sees a slim chance of a US-Iran deal and says the next two months carry the greatest escalation risk to Strait of Hormuz oil flows, while oil prices rose on renewed conflict fears. Iran is stepping up diplomacy, including with Russia and the UAE, and a rocket launcher deal reportedly illustrates deepening Russia-Iran ties. Iraq's prime minister spoke with Trump as Baghdad tries to stay out of any war, and there are fears in Israel over the future of US ties after the midterms.
topics.T15: Coverage is scattered and mostly single-source, with no single dominant event. Indonesia is dealing with a military helicopter crash during a wildfire response, with President Prabowo urging swift evacuation. Mount Bromo erupted Thursday, and East Java authorities are remapping evacuation routes. The rest is US flood and grid-reliability coverage, including local flooding in Brevard County, Florida, and a Puerto Rico resilience partnership.
topics.T01: Scores of flights across Europe received bomb threats this week with no explosives found, and a Russian extremist group has denied sending them; authorities have not confirmed who is responsible. An airstrike on a market in Yemen's Taiz province killed at least 30 people. Myanmar junta airstrikes killed five healthcare workers at a Sagaing hospital and three girls in Chin State. The UN Secretary-General voiced concern over possible escalation along the Korean DMZ, and analysts say a Trump-Xi-Putin meeting at APEC would favor Moscow while Beijing appears lukewarm.
topics.T02: Coverage is sparse and unconnected. South Sudan's health system is reportedly strained by refugee inflows from Sudan and foreign aid cuts. Education Cannot Wait received US$405.8 million in new pledges at a Geneva conference, bringing it to 90% of its target. Other items are an artwork naming children killed in Gaza and an upcoming Melbourne humanitarian law conference.
topics.T03: Quebec provincial police confirmed that a US army barrel found on an uninhabited St. Lawrence River island does not contain active anthrax, though the origin of the barrel remains a mystery. Separately, the White House finalized a policy to vet vendors of molecular materials to reduce the risk of AI-enabled bioweapons.
topics.T04: New World screwworm has been detected in 90 animals across Texas, New Mexico and Arizona, with an Arizona horse case prompting a 12.4-mile movement-control zone. Brazil confirmed a fourth Newcastle disease outbreak on a Santa Catarina poultry farm (the report's dates are internally inconsistent). Other animal-health items include lumpy skin disease at a Moscow-region farm, where about 800 carcasses were reportedly burned, and an anthrax outbreak killing hippos in an African park. A Ghana salmonella study is the only human-health item.
topics.T05: Stories are mixed and mostly single-source. Sudan and Ethiopia have expelled diplomats and closed consulates amid mutual accusations of backing armed groups. Self-styled 'king of Germany' Peter Fitzek is on trial for allegedly heading a criminal group. The remainder is commentary, including a piece claiming some evangelicals plan another January 6 and a historical retrospective on Bangladesh's Ziaur Rahman.
topics.T06: Thousands of French government workers, teachers and transport staff walked off the job Thursday over low wages and the cost of living. Other outlets describe French unrest as the country's biggest uprising since 1968, driven by students, and attribute some rioting to 'ultra-left' activists, though these are single-source accounts. Germany is debating integration after riots following Gen Z demonstrations, and Kosovo saw mass protests over the murder of Arlinda Zekaj. Smaller items cover Zurich riot sentences and Indian court proceedings tied to the Delhi riots case.
topics.T08: Syria condemned a terrorist attack in Amman that killed a Jordanian Public Security Directorate member and injured an officer. Malaysian police arrested at least 26 people after two riots in the Klang Valley. A Holocaust survivor wounded in the Bondi Beach terrorist attack has died a year later. The hoax bomb threats across Europe are covered under Military Conflict.
topics.T10: Coverage centers on rearmament spending and technology. Lockheed Martin won a $694 million US Air Force contract for an air-launched hypersonic missile, amid a reported US-China-Russia hypersonic race. Canada's budget charts $157 billion in annual defence spending by 2030, and the Pentagon is reportedly negotiating a 75-year rare earth purchase deal. Defense firms report continued demand for traditional equipment alongside drones and AI, while South Korean defense stocks have fallen in 2026.
topics.T11: Pakistan-Tajikistan counter-terrorism exercise Dosti-III concluded at Cherat. The Malabar naval exercise with Japan, the US, Australia and India has begun off Japan with a sub-hunting focus. India and Myanmar launched their first joint humanitarian assistance and disaster relief exercise, 'Rahat Mitra'. A Russian frigate also held its first anti-piracy exercise with Seychelles.
topics.T12: US authorities warned of an 'ongoing cyber threat' to industrial refrigeration systems, with at least three waves of attacks on commercial fridges and freezers in recent months. Cyberattacks reportedly disrupted supermarket refrigeration in Sweden, Belgium, Luxembourg, Ireland and Estonia on Nov. 2, forcing retailers to discard food. Other items include a DreamHost breach exposing customer data, a reported attack on Chainalysis tools, and a single-source claim that Binance lost $6.34 billion to North Korea-linked hackers. A fringe-site claim of a Paraguayan bank collapse is unverified.
topics.T13: Nearly 1,000 migrants were rescued from seven boats off El Hierro in Spain's Canary Islands, with about 700 to be moved to Tenerife to ease pressure on reception facilities. Other items are local: a Scottish council disputing an algorithm that allocates more asylum-seeking children, and a legal challenge to Denmark's 'non-Western ghettos' housing policy.
topics.T16: Democrats won commanding majorities in the House and Senate and a majority of governorships in the US midterms, prompting Republican infighting and 2028 positioning. South Africa's ANC faces a significant decline in support in early local election results. Myanmar will hold by-elections in April, including in areas of ongoing fighting, its first vote since a general election critics said was designed to cement military rule. In Israel, Netanyahu is reportedly using the Shin Bet to challenge an election his bloc lost, including seeking to question Arab party leaders over alleged foreign interference.

bluf: Thousands of French government workers, teachers and transport employees struck Thursday over low wages and the cost of living, in anti-government protests carried by four outlets. Ukrainian officials raised the Zaporizhia aid strike death toll to at least 50, with DNA tests being used to identify bodies and up to 39 people reportedly still under rubble. Scores of European flights have received bomb threats this week with no explosives found, and a Russian extremist group has denied sending them; authorities have not named a culprit. The US warned of an 'ongoing cyber threat' to industrial refrigeration systems after at least three waves of hacks on commercial fridges and freezers, and supermarket refrigeration was reportedly disrupted in five EU countries on Nov. 2. At Odesa's opera house, performances reportedly continue despite missile alerts and drone attacks, with audiences and performers sheltering during raids. Separately, President Trump is reportedly weighing renewed strikes on Iran after the midterm defeat, and FGE NexantECA says the next two months carry the highest escalation risk to Hormuz oil flows. Ursula von der Leyen is set to visit the Black Sea after at least seven commercial vessels were reportedly struck by drones that many link to Russia, ahead of US-mediated Ukraine-Russia talks in Abu Dhabi next week.
